target.title: cron: agent-scoped jobs can select another agent's delivery account
target.body:
## Summary
An agent-scoped cron caller can create or update a job whose `delivery.accountId` belongs to another agent. The job remains owned by the caller's agent, but scheduled messages are sent through the explicitly selected account and therefore through another agent's configured credentials and identity.

## Environment
- Commit: abfdfd65b850d63d75f80ac81f277272614b4745 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: model-facing cron tool, Gateway `cron.add` and `cron.update`, isolated cron announce delivery

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure two agents with bindings for the same channel: agent `ops` to account `ops-bot`, and agent `worker` to account `worker-bot`.
2. Invoke `cron.add` through a trusted internal agent-runtime connection scoped to agent `ops`.
3. Supply an isolated agent-turn job with `delivery.channel: "telegram"` and `delivery.accountId: "worker-bot"`.
4. Observe that the Gateway accepts the job, stamps `agentId: "ops"`, and preserves `delivery.accountId: "worker-bot"`.
5. Resolve the job's delivery target. Explicit `delivery.accountId` has highest precedence over the account bound to `ops`.

## Expected
An agent-scoped caller should only be able to select a delivery account bound to that caller's agent for the selected channel and target. A foreign account should be rejected before the job is persisted.

## Actual
The Gateway accepts the foreign account ID. At execution time the explicit account overrides both session-derived and binding-derived accounts, so delivery uses the other agent's channel identity.

## Root cause (if known)
`src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.ts:116` validates the job's effective agent and session references but does not inspect `job.delivery`:

```ts
export function cronCreateMatchesCallerScope(params: {
  job: CronJobCreate;
  callerScope: CronCallerScope | undefined;
  defaultAgentId?: string;
}): boolean {
  // ... agentId and session reference checks only
}
```

`src/cron/delivery-channel-validation.ts:81` validates delivery channel compatibility and configuration, but does not bind `delivery.accountId` to the caller agent.

`src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.ts:249` then gives the unbound value highest precedence:

```ts
// job.delivery.accountId takes highest precedence - explicitly set by the job author.
if (jobPayload.accountId) {
  accountId = jobPayload.accountId;
}
```

## Sibling surfaces
`cron.update` has the same gap: caller-scope validation blocks `agentId` and foreign session retargeting, but accepts a delivery patch containing a foreign account ID. PR #69518 proposed checking whether an account ID exists, but not whether it is bound to the caller's agent, and was closed without merge. PR #69940 was merged, but its account spoof guard only affects trace rewriting in `matchesMessagingToolDeliveryTarget`; it does not authorize cron delivery accounts.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: An agent-scoped cron caller can persist another agent's bound delivery account and the delivery resolver honors explicit account IDs over caller bindings.
Real environment tested: Production Gateway cron handler and production isolated delivery target resolver at commit abfdfd65b850d63d75f80ac81f277272614b4745.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran the focused Gateway cron handler reproduction together with the production delivery-target coverage using the repository runner and one worker.
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (buggy, origin/main abfdfd65b850d63d75f80ac81f277272614b4745)
AUDIT_CRON {"callerAgentId":"ops","storedAgentId":"ops","storedAccountId":"worker-bot","accepted":true}
Production resolver result for an explicit account over an agent binding: accountId="explicit"

# EXPECTED (correct behavior on identical input)
callerAgentId="ops"
stored=false
accepted=false
error="delivery.accountId is not bound to caller agent ops"
```
Observed result after fix: Current main accepts and persists a foreign bound account for an agent-scoped caller, and the delivery resolver gives the explicit account precedence.
What was not tested: No message was sent to a live external Telegram account. The channel adapter was kept at the outbound boundary; Gateway authorization, persistence input, binding lookup, and delivery target selection used production code.
